mainTopic: Selling large wild animals to non-Jews, tracing who first said the פירכוס rule, which basilicas may be built, and רבי אליעזר's arrest for מינות
overview: The amud opens by finishing the rejection of a proof for רב חנן בר רבא, who allowed selling a large wild animal to non-Jews. One answer says the משנה's lion is a maimed lion, following רבי יהודה. רב אשי says instead that an ordinary lion counts as maimed for work. A ברייתא then refutes רב חנן בר רבא, and the גמרא retells the discussion as רבינא's contradiction between the משנה and that ברייתא. רב נחמן then objects: who says a lion even counts as a large wild animal? רב אשי's close reading of the משנה refutes רב חנן בר רבא anyway, and wild donkeys turning millstones show that large wild animals can really work. Next, רבי זירא tells how he traced the rule that a חיה גסה is like a בהמה דקה for פירכוס back through a full chain of names to רב. The גמרא then explains the משנה's ban on building a בסילקי, with two versions of רבא. Finally, a ברייתא tells how רבי אליעזר was arrested for מינות, acquitted, and stayed troubled; רבי עקיבא's suggestion to him continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The proof fails: the lion in the משנה is maimed, following רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of the answer that pushes away the proof for רב חנן בר רבא. The משנה's lion is a maimed lion, and the case follows רבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this follows the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to the attempted proof. The משנה can be read as talking about a maimed lion, under רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof said: the משנה forbids lions only because of damage, so a harmless large wild animal may be sold. The answer is that the משנה's lion is maimed and cannot work. רבי יהודה (משנה on 14b) allows selling a maimed large animal, so the only problem left is damage. A healthy large wild animal could still be forbidden because it can do work.

keyTerms.meaning: a maimed (broken) lion that cannot do work

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the tail of an answer that began before this section. It is not a new statement, and the words 'a maimed lion' came just before it.

phrases.english: And this follows the view of רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection of the proof for רב חנן בר רבא, which came just before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the משנה, not רב חנן בר רבא's position itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה is about a healthy lion. It may be about a maimed lion, where only damage matters.

steps.title: רב אשי: an ordinary lion counts as maimed for work
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי pushes the proof away differently. Every ordinary lion is considered 'maimed' when it comes to work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: An ordinary lion is considered maimed with regard to work.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives another way to push away the proof from the משנה. We do not need a special maimed lion, because lions are not used for work at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual reason not to sell large animals is the worry that they will be made to work on שבת. Lions are never put to work, so a normal lion is like a maimed animal in this respect. That is why the משנה mentions only damage, and the proof for רב חנן בר רבא falls away again.

keyTerms.meaning: with regard to, when it comes to

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
An ordinary lion is maimed
with regard to work.
phrases.notes: He means lions aren't used as work animals, so for this law a healthy lion is treated like a broken one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: סְתָם אֲרִי שָׁבוּר הוּא אֵצֶל מְלָאכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reason why the משנה does not prove רב חנן בר רבא's view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה mentions only damage because a lion has no work concern at all, not because large wild animals are generally allowed.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids selling large wild animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חנן בר רבא with a ברייתא. It says large wild animals are forbidden just like large livestock.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: Just as one may not sell them large livestock, so one may not sell them large wild animals. And even in a place where people sell them small livestock, one may not sell them large wild animals.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא attacks רב חנן בר רבא directly with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says large wild animals may never be sold to non-Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חנן בר רבא compared large wild animals to small livestock, which is allowed in places with that custom. The ברייתא says the opposite: even where small livestock is sold, large wild animals are not. So large wild animals belong with large livestock.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין מוֹכְרִין לָהֶן בְּהֵמָה גַּסָּה,
phrases.english: Just as one may not sell them large livestock,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אֵין מוֹכְרִין לָהֶן חַיָּה גַּסָּה,
phrases.english: so too one may not sell them large wild animals,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁמּוֹכְרִין לָהֶן בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה —
phrases.english: and even in a place where they sell them small livestock,
large wild animals one may not sell them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof for רב חנן בר רבא was pushed away, the גמרא now brings a source against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חנן בר רבא's ruling that a large wild animal is like small livestock.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly separates large wild animals from small livestock and groups them with large livestock, which is forbidden.

steps.title: רב חנן בר רבא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is a full refutation of רב חנן בר רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רב חנן בר רבא; it is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא declares that רב חנן בר רבא's view is refuted. No answer is offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא is a תנאי source, and an אמורא cannot argue against it. The ברייתא openly contradicts רב חנן בר רבא, so his ruling is rejected. Large wild animals may not be sold.
steps.whatToRemember: In this first version, large wild animals may not be sold to non-Jews, just like large livestock. רב חנן בר רבא's lenient view is refuted.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of רב חנן בר רבא;
it is a refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא, תְּיוּבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of the ברייתא's challenge.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב חנן בר רבא is refuted: large wild animals are treated like large livestock and may not be sold.

steps.title: רבינא's version begins: he quotes the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a second version. רבינא sets the משנה against a ברייתא, starting with the משנה about bears and lions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא set the משנה against a ברייתא and resolved it. We learned: One may not sell them bears or lions, or anything that can cause damage to the public.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup step for a new version of the discussion. רבינא will show a clash between our משנה and a ברייתא, and he starts by quoting the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version nobody named רב חנן בר רבא is involved. The same material is framed as a contradiction between two תנאי sources that needs to be settled. The משנה quoted here gives the reason for forbidding bears and lions: they can hurt the public.

keyTerms.meaning: sets one source against another (raises a contradiction)
a תנאי teaching not included in the משנה

phrases.english: רבינא set the משנה against a ברייתא and resolved it:
We learned in the משנה:
One may not sell them bears or lions

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ נֶזֶק לָרַבִּים,
phrases.english: or anything that can cause damage to the public.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא רָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין אַבָּרַיְיתָא וּמְשַׁנֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the whole discussion, framed as רבינא's contradiction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה forbids selling bears, lions, and anything that endangers the public.

steps.title: Inference from the משנה: harmless animals may be sold
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reads the משנה closely. The only reason given is damage, so an animal that causes no damage may be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that it causes damage. But if it does not cause damage, one may sell it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא draws an inference from the wording of the משנה. This sets up one side of the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names damage as the problem with lions. That suggests a large wild animal that is not dangerous would be allowed. This inference is what will clash with the ברייתא.

phrases.english: The reason is that it causes damage;
but if it does not cause damage, one may sell it.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ נֶזֶק, הָא לֵית בֵּיהּ נֶזֶק מוֹכְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the key inference from the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By implication, a large wild animal that causes no damage may be sold.

steps.title: The ברייתא contradicts the inference
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings the ברייתא that forbids selling any large wild animal. This contradicts the inference from the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he contrasted it: Just as one may not sell large livestock, so one may not sell large wild animals. And even in a place where they sell small livestock, one may not sell large wild animals.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא shows the other side of the contradiction. The same ברייתא from before says large wild animals are always forbidden, even when harmless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה suggests a harmless large wild animal may be sold. The ברייתא says it may not, because large wild animals are like large livestock. These two sources seem to disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: and he raised a contradiction against it

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same ברייתא as in step 3, but here it is used to create a contradiction with the משנה. It is not used to refute an אמורא.

phrases.english: And he contrasted it with this:
Just as one may not sell large livestock,
so too one may not sell large wild animals,
and even in a place where they sell small livestock,
large wild animals one may not sell.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the ברייתא against the inference drawn from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from the משנה that harmless large wild animals may be sold.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids all large wild animals regardless of danger, which contradicts the משנה's implied permission.

steps.title: Resolution: the משנה speaks of a maimed lion, following רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא settles the clash. The משנה is about a maimed lion, following רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he resolved it: The משנה is about a maimed lion, and it follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers his own contradiction. He limits the משנה to a maimed lion that cannot work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי יהודה, a maimed large animal may be sold because it cannot be used for work. For such a lion the only issue left is damage, which is why the משנה mentions only damage. The ברייתא, which forbids large wild animals, is talking about healthy ones, so the two sources no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: limiting a source to a specific case in order to resolve a difficulty
the case is about a maimed lion
a maimed animal, which רבי יהודה allows to be sold

phrases.english: And he resolved it: it is about a maimed lion,
and it follows the view of רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְשַׁנֵּי: בַּאֲרִי שָׁבוּר, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: אוקימתא: limiting the משנה to a specific case (a maimed lion) under a specific תנא (רבי יהודה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to allow selling any harmless large wild animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה allows only a maimed lion, where work is not a concern. Healthy large wild animals remain forbidden, as the ברייתא says.

steps.title: רב אשי's alternative: any ordinary lion counts as maimed for work
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי resolves the contradiction differently. Every ordinary lion is considered maimed when it comes to work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: An ordinary lion is considered maimed with regard to work.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second way to settle רבינא's contradiction. No special maimed lion is needed, because lions are not used for work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on selling large animals comes from the worry about them doing work, such as on שבת. Lions are not used for work, so for them the only issue is damage, and that is all the משנה mentions. The ברייתא's ban covers large wild animals that can do work.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree that large wild animals generally may not be sold. A lion is forbidden only because of public danger: it is either maimed (following רבי יהודה) or, as רב אשי says, lions never do work in the first place.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:

phrases.aramaic: סְתָם אֲרִי שָׁבוּר הוּא אֵצֶל מְלָאכָה.
phrases.english: An ordinary lion is maimed with regard to work.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: סְתָם אֲרִי שָׁבוּר הוּא אֵצֶל מְלָאכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the same contradiction resolved in step 8. The גמרא really does repeat רב אשי's words here, inside רבינא's version.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition: an ordinary lion falls into the 'maimed for work' group, with no need to limit the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think only a specially maimed lion would escape the work concern.
steps.terutzMaskana: All lions lack the work concern, so the משנה mentions only damage. The ברייתא's ban applies to large wild animals that can work.

steps.title: Is a lion really a large wild animal?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן questions whether a lion counts as a חיה גסה at all. Maybe it is a small wild animal (חיה דקה).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן objects: Who says a lion is a large wild animal? Maybe it is a small wild animal!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks the idea that the lion in the משנה tells us anything about large wild animals. He suggests a lion might be classified as a small wild animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier reading used the lion to learn a rule about every חיה גסה. If a lion is really a חיה דקה, the משנה says nothing about large wild animals. Then the inference falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (a strong challenge)

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman objects to it:
Who will tell us
that a lion is a large wild animal?
Perhaps it is a small wild animal!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind the earlier reading that a lion counts as a חיה גסה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that the lion case in the משנה teaches a rule about large wild animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a lion is really a חיה דקה, nothing can be learned from it about חיה גסה.

steps.title: רב אשי reads the משנה: no damage means selling is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי sets up a refutation by reading the משנה closely. The only reason it gives is public damage, so an animal that does no damage may be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי read the משנה carefully and raised a refutation. We learned: One may not sell them bears, lions, or anything that causes damage to the public. The reason is that it causes damage. But if it does not cause damage, one may sell it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up רב אשי's refutation. It first quotes the משנה and draws his first inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids bears and lions only because they endanger the public. So an animal that causes no damage would be allowed. This first inference is not the refutation itself; it prepares the second inference in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Reads closely / makes a precise inference

phrases.english: Rav Ashi read the mishnah closely
and raises a refutation,
we learned:
One may not sell them bears and lions

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ נֶזֶק לָרַבִּים.
phrases.english: nor anything that causes damage to the public.
The reason is that it causes damage,
but if it causes no damage, one may sell it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי דָּיֵיק מַתְנִיתִין וּמוֹתֵיב תְּיוּבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב נחמן's objection in step 10. רב אשי's reading does not depend on whether a lion is a חיה גסה. It rests on the משנה's stated reason (damage) and on the fact that a lion does no work, and that reading turns into a refutation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the משנה: an animal that causes no public damage may be sold.

steps.title: Lions are allowed only because they can't work
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי's second inference: a harmless lion is allowed only because lions are useless for work. Any animal that does work may not be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the reason a lion is allowed is that an ordinary lion is 'broken' when it comes to work. But a different animal that does work may not be sold.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why the משנה picked a lion for its example. That reasoning creates a problem for רב חנן בר רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lion is allowed only because an ordinary lion can't do work. So any animal that can work, including a working חיה גסה, may not be sold. That clashes with רב חנן בר רבא, who allowed selling large wild animals.
steps.confusionAlert: This does NOT say lions may be sold freely. The משנה still forbids dangerous lions. The point is only that a harmless lion is allowed because it can't work, while working animals stay forbidden.

phrases.english: And the reason a lion is allowed

phrases.aramaic: דִּסְתָם אֲרִי שָׁבוּר הוּא אֵצֶל מְלָאכָה,
phrases.english: is that an ordinary lion is 'broken' when it comes to work,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִידֵּי אַחֲרִינָא דְּעָבֵיד מְלָאכָה — לָא.
phrases.english: but a different animal that does work — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטַעְמָא אֲרִי, דִּסְתָם אֲרִי שָׁבוּר הוּא אֵצֶל מְלָאכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב אשי's reading. The second inference produces the actual challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חנן בר רבא's ruling that a חיה גסה may be sold.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lion is allowed only because it can't work. So any working animal, including a working חיה גסה, is forbidden.

steps.title: רב חנן בר רבא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares that רב חנן בר רבא's view is conclusively refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The refutation of רב חנן בר רבא is a conclusive refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this argument. רב חנן בר רבא's view is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's reading shows the משנה forbids selling any animal that can work. That leaves no room for permitting a working חיה גסה, so the opposing view is dropped.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation; when repeated, it means a final, conclusive refutation

steps.whatToRemember: The conclusion: a large wild animal that can do work may not be sold. A lion is allowed (when it isn't dangerous) only because lions are unfit for work.

phrases.english: The refutation of Rav Ḥanan bar Rava
is a conclusive refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא, תְּיוּבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules that the challenge in step 12 stands.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב חנן בר רבא is refuted. A working חיה גסה may not be sold.

steps.title: What work can a large wild animal do?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what work a large wild animal could possibly do, so that it would need to be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And anyway, what work does a large wild animal do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question that sets up the next line. Wild animals aren't usually trained to work, so why forbid selling them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling only makes sense if some large wild animals actually do work. The גמרא wants a real-life example.

phrases.english: And a large wild animal, anyway,
what work does it do?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַיָּה גַּסָּה מִיהַת מַאי מְלָאכָה עָבְדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the conclusion of step 13 could apply in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A real example of a large wild animal that does work.

steps.title: Wild donkeys turning millstones
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports from מר יהודה that in מר יוחני's household, wild donkeys were used to grind at the mill.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: מר יהודה told me that in the house of מר יוחני they grind with millstones using wild donkeys.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question with a real example. Wild donkeys, which count as large wild animals, were put to work turning millstones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that some large wild animals really can work. So the ban on selling working animals truly applies to them.

keyTerms.meaning: In the house of / the household of

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns the rule into something real. A working חיה גסה is an actual case, not just theory.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Mar Yehuda told me
that in the house of Mar Yoḥani
they grind with millstones using wild donkeys.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אֲמַר לִי מָר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wild donkeys, which are large wild animals, were used to turn millstones.

steps.title: רב יהודה teaches a rule about large wild animals but forgets who said it
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reports that רב יהודה taught that a חיה גסה is like a בהמה דקה for פירכוס. רב יהודה heard it from a great man but did not know if it was רב or שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: When we were in רב יהודה's study hall, he told us: Learn this from me. I heard it from a great man, but I don't know if it was רב or שמואל: a large wild animal is like small livestock when it comes to the sign-of-life movement.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא brings a new הלכה about large wild animals. He also starts a story about finding out who first said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says a חיה גסה is judged like a בהמה דקה for the movement that shows the animal was alive at שחיטה. The open question here is not the rule itself but who said it, רב or שמואל. That question drives the whole story that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Small livestock, like sheep and goats
The movement or spasm at slaughter that shows the animal was still alive
A great man, meaning a major Torah scholar

steps.whyThisMatters: The story shows how carefully the חכמים worked to say a teaching in the name of the person who really said it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
When we were in the study hall of Rav Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַן: גְּמִירוּ מִינַּאי הָא מִילְּתָא,
phrases.english: he said to us: Learn from me this matter,
which I heard from a great man,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא יָדַעְנָא אִי מֵרַב אִי מִשְּׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: but I do not know if it was from Rav or from Shmuel:
A large wild animal is
like small livestock with regard to the spasm.
phrases.notes: פירכוס is the twitch or movement at שחיטה that shows the animal was still alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: כִּי הֲוֵינַן בֵּי רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of large wild animals (like the wild donkeys of step 15) with a new הלכה about them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חיה גסה is treated like a בהמה דקה for פירכוס. Who said it, רב or שמואל, is unknown.

steps.title: In קורקוניא, the rule is heard in שמואל's name
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא finds רב חייא בר אשי teaching the same rule in the name of שמואל. He concludes that it was said by שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I came to קורקוניא, I found רב חייא בר אשי sitting and saying in the name of שמואל: a large wild animal is like small livestock for the spasm. I said: this shows it was said in the name of שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא hears the same rule in a new place, said in שמואל's name. He takes this as evidence for who said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's doubt was between רב and שמואל. Here a clear report says שמואל, so רבי זירא thinks the question is settled.

phrases.english: When I came to Korkoneya,
I found Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi
sitting and saying in the name of Shmuel:
A large wild animal is
like small livestock with regard to the spasm.
I said: Learn from this
that it was stated in the name of Shmuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתַאי לְקוּרְקוּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first answer to רב יהודה's doubt about who said the rule.
steps.raayaObject: Who first said the rule about חיה גסה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חייא בר אשי's report in the name of שמואל

steps.title: In סורא, the rule is heard in רב's name too
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר ירמיה teaches the same rule in the name of רב. רבי זירא concludes that it was said by both רב and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I came to סורא, I found רבה בר ירמיה sitting and saying it in the name of רב: a large wild animal is like small livestock for the spasm. I said: this shows it was said in the name of רב, and also in the name of שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבי זירא hears the same rule in רב's name. He decides that both great teachers said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first it looked like only שמואל said it. A second report in רב's name makes רבי זירא add רב as well, instead of picking one.

keyTerms.meaning: סורא, the city of רב's great ישיבה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא is not saying the first report was wrong. He keeps שמואל and adds רב, so for now the rule is said by both.

phrases.english: When I came to Sura,
I found Rabba bar Yirmeya
sitting and saying it in the name of Rav:
A large wild animal is
like small livestock with regard to the spasm.
I said: Learn from this
that it was stated in the name of Rav
and it was stated in the name of Shmuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתַאי לְסוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second report and widens the conclusion: both רב and שמואל said the rule.
steps.raayaObject: That רב also said the rule
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה בר ירמיה's report in the name of רב

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל, רב אסי quotes the rule through רב חמא בר גוריא
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי teaches the rule in the name of רב חמא בר גוריא, quoting רב. This sets up רבי זירא's question about רבה בר ירמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I went up there, I found רב אסי sitting and saying: רב חמא בר גוריא said in the name of רב: a large wild animal is like small livestock for the spasm.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא hears the rule yet again, now with a different person in the middle of the chain. This sets up his question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the report in סורא, this one also goes back to רב. But it names רב חמא בר גוריא as the one who passed it on, not רבה בר ירמיה. That difference is what bothers רבי זירא.

keyTerms.meaning: I went up there, meaning to ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: When I ascended to there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means ארץ ישראל. People speak of going 'up' to it.

phrases.english: I found Rav Asi sitting and saying:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said in the name of Rav:
A large wild animal is
like small livestock with regard to the spasm.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סְלֵיקִית לְהָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third report. It agrees that the rule comes from רב but names a different person who passed it on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חמא בר גוריא passed on the rule in the name of רב.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks why רבה בר ירמיה is not mentioned
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רב אסי: isn't רבה בר ירמיה the one this teaching comes from? Why quote רב חמא בר גוריא instead?
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: Doesn't the master agree that the master of this teaching is רבה בר ירמיה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges רב אסי's chain of names. In סורא he heard the rule from רבה בר ירמיה, so why does רב אסי leave him out?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two reports do not match on who passed on רב's words. רבי זירא points this out and suggests that רבה בר ירמיה should be the one named.

keyTerms.meaning: The master of the teaching, the one it comes from
Master, a polite way to say 'you'

phrases.english: I said to him:
And doesn't the Master hold

phrases.aramaic: דְּמַאן מָרָא דִּשְׁמַעְתְּתָא רַבָּה בַּר יִרְמְיָה?
phrases.english: that the master of this teaching is Rabba bar Yirmeya?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that the chains of names in steps 18 and 19 do not match.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's chain of names, which skips רבה בר ירמיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי זירא heard the teaching in רב's name from רבה בר ירמיה, so naming רב חמא בר גוריא instead seems wrong.

steps.title: רב אסי answers: put our two reports together
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי affectionately calls רבי זירא 'black pot' and says the full chain comes from combining what each of them knows.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: Black pot! From me and from you the teaching will be complete.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי answers that both reports are true, and each one fills in part of the chain. Put together, they give the full chain of who said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא knew רבה בר ירמיה's part, and רב אסי knew רב חמא בר גוריא's part. Both are links in one chain going back to רב, so neither report is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Black pot, a loving nickname for a hard-working Torah scholar

phrases.english: He said to me: Black pot,
phrases.notes: A warm nickname, not an insult. It praises someone who works hard at learning Torah.

phrases.english: from me and from you the teaching will be completed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לִי: פַּתְיָא אוּכָּמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by joining the two chains instead of choosing one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Joining two partial reports into one chain
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two chains seemed to clash, so one would have to be wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each report is one part of a single chain. Together they show the full path back to רב.

steps.title: The full chain of names is stated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a statement giving the complete chain: רבי זירא, from רב אסי, from רבה בר ירמיה, from רב חמא בר גוריא, from רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי זירא said that רב אסי said that רבה בר ירמיה said that רב חמא בר גוריא said that רב said: a large wild animal is like small livestock for the spasm.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא confirms the joined chain from step 21 by quoting it in full. This closes the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every name from both reports now appears in one line, ending with רב. This shows that רב אסי's answer was right: the teaching comes from רב, passed on through both scholars.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated, used to bring a supporting statement

steps.whatToRemember: A חיה גסה is treated like a בהמה דקה for פירכוס. The confirmed chain is רבי זירא, from רב אסי, from רבה בר ירמיה, from רב חמא בר גוריא, from רב.

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא, אָמַר רַב אַסִּי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Asi said
that Rabba bar Yirmeya said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
A large wild animal is
like small livestock with regard to the spasm.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms step 21's joined chain by quoting it in full.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rule comes from רב through רב חמא בר גוריא, then רבה בר ירמיה, then רב אסי, then רבי זירא.

steps.title: Three types of basilica
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן: there are three kinds of בסילקי, belonging to kings, to bathhouses, and to storehouses.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the משנה's rule 'one may not build...': רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן that there are three kinds of basilicas: those of kings, those of bathhouses, and those of storehouses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about building a בסילקי and brings רבי יוחנן's list of three types. This list sets up רבא's ruling on which types are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just said 'בסילקי' without explaining it. רבי יוחנן shows that the word covers different buildings with different uses. So the next question is whether the איסור covers all of them or only some.

phrases.english: One may not build, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה's rule against building a basilica together with גוים.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
There are three kinds of basilicas:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל מְלָכִים, וְשֶׁל מֶרְחֲצָאוֹת, וְשֶׁל אוֹצָרוֹת.
phrases.english: those of kings, and those of bathhouses, and those of storehouses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: explaining the משנה's word בסילקי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word בסילקי covers three types: of kings, of bathhouses, and of storehouses.

steps.title: Two types permitted, one forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that two types of בסילקי are permitted and one is forbidden. He gives a memory aid from a פסוק about binding kings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: two are permitted and one is forbidden. The memory aid is the פסוק 'To bind their kings with chains.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא says which of רבי יוחנן's three types may be built. He gives a פסוק to help remember that the kings' basilica is the forbidden one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kings' basilica is where people were judged and sentenced, so helping build it is forbidden. Bathhouse and storehouse basilicas have no such use, so they are permitted. The word לאסר ('to bind') sounds like לאיסור ('forbidden'), and the פסוק mentions kings.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Two are permitted and one is forbidden,
and the memory aid is: “To bind their kings with chains.”
phrases.notes: תהלים 149:8. 'To bind' sounds like 'forbidden,' and it goes with 'kings,' so the kings' basilica is the forbidden one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁתַּיִם לְהֶיתֵּר וְאֶחָד לְאִיסּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the הלכה for each of the three types רבי יוחנן listed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The basilica of kings is forbidden. The basilicas of bathhouses and storehouses are permitted.

steps.title: Another version: all three permitted
steps.stepSummary: Some report רבא differently: according to them, he permitted all three types of בסילקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say that רבא said: all of them are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of what רבא said, in which every type of basilica is allowed. This sets up a challenge from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version even the kings' basilica is permitted. That seems to clash with the משנה, which plainly lists בסילקי as forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In the first, רבא forbids the kings' basilica. In this one, he permits all three.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
Rava said: All of them are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רָבָא: כּוּלָּם לְהֶיתֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing report of רבא's ruling from step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All three types of basilica are permitted.

steps.title: The משנה forbids basilicas
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second version: the משנה explicitly says one may not build a בסילקי with גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: one may not build with them a basilica, a tribunal, a stadium, or a platform!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the version where רבא permits all basilicas by quoting the משנה, which lists בסילקי as forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every basilica were permitted, the משנה could not list 'basilica' among the forbidden buildings. So it looks like this version of רבא contradicts a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A tribunal, where people were sentenced

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the mishna:
One may not build with them a basilica,
a tribunal, a stadium, or a platform!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: אֵין בּוֹנִין עִמָּהֶן בָּסִילְקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the version of רבא in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The version of רבא that says all basilicas are permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lists בסילקי by itself as forbidden, so not all basilicas can be permitted.

steps.title: Read it as a basilica of a tribunal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by reading the משנה differently: it forbids a basilica that serves as a tribunal, a stadium, or a platform, not every basilica.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it like this: a basilica of a tribunal, of a stadium, or of a platform.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by rereading the משנה's list. 'Basilica' is not its own item; it describes what follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the משנה seemed to list four separate forbidden things. Now the next three words tell us which kind of basilica is forbidden: one used for a tribunal, stadium, or platform. A plain basilica is allowed, so רבא's 'all permitted' fits.

keyTerms.meaning: Say: read the text this way

phrases.english: Say:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל גַּרְדּוֹם וְשֶׁל אִיצְטַדְיָיא וְשֶׁל בִּימָה.
phrases.english: a basilica of a tribunal, or of a stadium, or of a platform.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: שֶׁל גַּרְדּוֹם וְשֶׁל אִיצְטַדְיָיא וְשֶׁל בִּימָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה lists 'basilica' as its own forbidden item.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה forbids only a basilica used as a tribunal, stadium, or platform. Other basilicas are permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: In one version of רבא, only the kings' basilica is forbidden. In the other, any basilica is permitted unless it serves as a גרדום, stadium, or platform.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר brought to trial for heresy
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that רבי אליעזר was arrested for מינות and brought to a גרדום. The officer asked why an old sage like him would get involved in such nonsense.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: When רבי אליעזר was arrested for heresy, they brought him up to the tribunal to be judged. That officer said to him: Should an old man like you busy himself with these worthless things?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the משנה mentioned a גרדום, the גמרא tells a story about רבי אליעזר being judged on one. This step sets up the scene and the officer's question, which רבי אליעזר answers next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The link is the word גרדום, the place where people were sentenced. The officer's question is not a real accusation. He seems surprised that a respected elder would get involved in מינות, which opens the door for רבי אליעזר's answer.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
When Rabbi Eliezer was arrested for heresy,
they brought him up to the tribunal to be judged.
That officer said to him:
Should an elder like you busy himself
with these worthless matters?
phrases.notes: He means the heresy that רבי אליעזר was accused of.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כְּשֶׁנִּתְפַּס רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְמִינוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connected by the word גרדום from the משנה quoted in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר was brought to a גרדום on a charge of מינות and questioned by the officer.

steps.title: 'The Judge is trustworthy to me'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that he trusts the Judge. The officer thinks he means him, but רבי אליעזר really means הקב״ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The Judge is trustworthy to me. That officer thought he was talking about him, but he really meant only his Father in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers the officer with words that have two meanings. The officer takes them one way, and רבי אליעזר means them another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The Judge' could mean the officer sitting in judgment, or ה׳, the true Judge. The officer heard it as flattery and trust in him. רבי אליעזר meant that he accepts ה׳'s judgment.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר did not praise the Roman officer. 'The Judge' he meant was ה׳. Only the officer thought it was about him.

phrases.english: He said to him: The Judge is trustworthy to me.

phrases.aramaic: כְּסָבוּר אוֹתוֹ הֶגְמוֹן: עָלָיו הוּא אוֹמֵר,
phrases.english: That officer thought he was speaking about him,
but he said it only
in reference to his Father in Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: נֶאֱמָן עָלַי הַדַּיָּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אליעזר's reply to the officer's question in step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why would an elder like רבי אליעזר get involved in heresy?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He says he trusts 'the Judge', meaning ה׳, though the officer thinks it means him.

steps.title: The officer acquits רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: Thinking רבי אליעזר trusts him, the officer declares him acquitted and free.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Since you trusted me, you are acquitted, you are free.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the officer setting רבי אליעזר free because of how he understood the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The officer took the answer as a sign of trust and respect, and he rewarded it with acquittal. רבי אליעזר's careful words saved him without saying anything false.

phrases.english: He said to him: Since you have trusted me,
acquitted — you are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: הוֹאִיל וְהֶאֱמַנְתִּי עָלֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The result of the officer misunderstanding רבי אליעזר's words in step 29.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אליעזר was acquitted because the officer thought רבי אליעזר trusted him.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר refuses to be comforted
steps.stepSummary: When רבי אליעזר comes home, his students come to comfort him, but he will not accept their comfort.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came home, his students came in to comfort him, and he did not accept their comfort.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward: רבי אליעזר is home, his students try to comfort him, and he refuses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He was found not guilty, yet he is still upset. His refusal shows that being arrested for מינות bothers him even after he was freed. This sets up רבי עקיבא's attempt to explain why it happened.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the story is over because he was freed in step 30. Being acquitted did not end his distress, and the rest of the story deals with that.

phrases.english: When he came to his home,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אליעזר, who has just been set free by the officer.

phrases.english: his students came in to him to comfort him,
and he did not accept comfort.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁבָּא לְבֵיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the arrest story after his release in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after being freed, רבי אליעזר stays upset about being arrested for מינות and will not be comforted.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא asks permission to speak
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא respectfully asks his teacher if he may say one thing he learned from him, and רבי אליעזר says yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: My teacher, will you allow me to say one thing from what you taught me? He said to him: Speak.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא asks permission to share a thought, and רבי אליעזר agrees. This is preparing the next move, where רבי עקיבא gives his suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא is about to say something hard to hear, so he asks permission first. He presents it as coming from רבי אליעזר's own teaching, which makes it easier to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: Will you allow me / give me permission

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him: My teacher,
will you allow me to say one thing
from what you taught me?
He said to him: Speak.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: רַבִּי, תַּרְשֵׁינִי לוֹמַר דָּבָר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי אליעזר's refusal to be comforted by offering to explain something.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Permission to say one idea he learned from his teacher.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא suggests heresy once came before him
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא begins to suggest that perhaps some word of מינות once came before רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My teacher, perhaps some מינות came before you
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא starts giving his explanation: maybe רבי אליעזר once came into contact with מינות. The sentence continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא is suggesting a reason why רבי אליעזר was arrested for מינות. Maybe it is connected to some earlier contact with מינות. The full idea, and רבי אליעזר's reaction, come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Came to your hand, meaning came before you

phrases.english: He said to him: My teacher,
perhaps some heresy came to your hand

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: רַבִּי, שֶׁמָּא מִינוּת בָּא לְיָדְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא uses the permission he received in step 32 to begin his suggestion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא suggests that maybe רבי אליעזר once came into contact with מינות. The explanation continues past this point.
